To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) High fat diets, coupled with a lack of exercise, induce mitochondrial dysfunction in skeletal muscle, heart and liver, which are associated with a decrease in the abundance of the unique mitochondrial membrane phospholipid cardiolipin; 2) The decrease in cardiolipin abundance, in turn, is associated with a decrease of the mitochondrial electron transport chain complex activity, which is associated with the decrease of the respiratory chain complexes activity, and a decrease in ATP production; 3
high lipid intake and related disorders, including obesity, insulin resistance and hepatic steatostis, are associated with a decrease in the abundance of CL in the heart, liver and skeletal muscle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CL as a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of obesity and related metabolic disorders.
the impact of lipid overload and the related metabolic alterations on the abundance and form of the mitochondrial specific phospholipid CL in the heart, skeletal muscle and liver.
the effects of dietary lipid intake and metabolic disorders on CL abundance and acyl chain composition in the major energy producing organs, heart, muscle and the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the abundance and acylation of CL in the heart, skeletal muscle and liver are altered following high dietary lipid supplementation and the associated metabolic disorders.
high dietary lipid intake, and the related metabolic diseases, lead to a significant decrease in CL abundance and a change in the acyl composition of CL.

the abundance and form of CL are altered in the major metabolic organs of obese and diabetic animal models, and that these changes may contribute to the mitochondrial dysfunction observed in the metabolic syndrome and related diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CL abundance is decreased in the liver and heart of mice that are fed a high fat diet, while CL is increased in skeletal muscle.
high dietary lipid intake induces a reduction in CL abundance, with an associated change in its acyl profile, in the major metabolic organs.
CL content and acylation is highly sensitive to dietary lipid overload and related metabolic disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CL abundance and form are altered by the metabolic state of the cell, which in turn may have a profound impact on mitochondrial function.

CL abundance and composition is affected by both high fat feeding and related metabolic diseases, and that these alterations may contribute to the development of mitochondrial dysfunction in these tissues.
CL content and acylation are altered in all tissues following a high fat diet and in liver and skeletal muscle of diabetic rats.
